item.text: Chrome is running, so I’m going to use its live settings/profile data carefully rather than relying on a stale edit that Chrome might overwrite on exit. First I’m checking how the current search-provider entries are stored.

item.text: The profile does not currently have an explicit user-level default search provider, and Chrome protects that setting with its secure preferences hash. I’m going to use Chrome’s supported managed policy mechanism, which is reliable for this and survives restarts.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'which google-chrome || which google-chrome-stable || which chromium || true'

item.text: The Bing policy is installed. I’m restarting Chrome now so the address bar uses the new search provider immediately instead of waiting for Chrome’s policy refresh interval.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "pkill -TERM -f '/opt/google/chrome/chrome' || true
sleep 2
nohup google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=1337 >/tmp/chrome-restart.log 2>&1 &
sleep 3
ps -ef | rg -i '[c]hrome --remote-debugging-port|[c]hrome"'$'"'"
